title: Is TJX Stock an Undervalued Stock to Buy Right Now?
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; one spot garbled (forward-PE figure not captured in captions)
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc evaluates TJX Companies (TJ Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods), one of the few brick-and-mortar retailers still growing. Management raised its long-term store target by 500 units to 7,500 and is accelerating expansion to ~4% per year. TTM revenue topped $62B, more than double the ~$30B in 2017, driven by the off-price 'treasure hunt' model; Ross and Burlington show the category strength is industry-wide. TTM operating margin of ~12.5% is a decade high but the industry is not very lucrative given store/personnel/inventory costs. ROIC is a strong 26% TTM (~20% decade average), well above WACC, so the accelerated store investment should add shareholder value. His DCF values the business at ~$102 per share vs a $131 market price — roughly 10-15% overvalued after his usual 5-10% margin of safety — while the forward P/E is below the stock's two-year average (the exact figure was garbled in captions). He last covered TJX on May 5, 2025 with a non-buy stance, and that call worked: the stock is down ~6% since vs the S&P 500 up ~20%. Today he reiterates a HOLD: not ridiculously expensive, no need to dump, but better risk/reward exists elsewhere and he would wait for a better entry point. Call: TJX — HOLD @ $131 (DCF $102).

calls.thesis: Reiterated hold: 10-15% overvalued vs DCF even with margin of safety; better opportunities elsewhere, no need to dump.
calls.base_case: Strong ROIC (~26%), accelerating store expansion from 7,000 to 7,500 units.
calls.bull_case: Off-price demand stays strong; expansion compounds shareholder value.
calls.bear_case: Incremental dollar gets better risk/reward elsewhere; overvaluation persists.
